主要内容: A new study suggests that private companies outperform public utilities in meeting regulations. The research, set to be published in the American Journal of Political Science, highlights that private utilities, which serve investors rather than a constituency, can more effectively manage infrastructure upgrades and regulatory compliance. In contrast, public utilities often struggle with funding and face leniency from regulators, which can hinder their ability to meet federal standards. The study also notes that private utilities can set rates based on investment costs, potentially impacting low-income consumers. This analysis underscores the trade-offs between public and private utility models in terms of regulatory performance and financial sustainability.
